content: There is no more valuable precept in moral education than this: smooth the brow, brighten the eye, contract the dorsal rather than the ventral aspect of the frame, and speak in a major key.
author: William James
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, William James saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
